title: Home Reno - Studio
summary: Original floors, exposed shiplap, and a repaired plank ceiling give a former living room a new purpose.
searchSummary: Living-room-to-ballet-barre-studio restoration: reclaimed ceiling planks, hand-scraped and sanded original floors, brushed polyurethane, exposed shiplap, lime paint and slurry, and coped crown molding.
stage: Near-completion in the August 30 journal; final studio sign-off not documented
sourceLabel: Studio restoration journal and Home Reno - Studio Google Photos album

gallery.caption: The Studio nearing completion on August 26, 2026: exposed wood flooring, painted walls and ceiling, and the retained timber wall.
gallery.alt: A light wood floor extends beneath white walls and a white plank ceiling, with tall windows and a dark door in the timber wall.

gallery.caption: The former living room at the start of the recorded work, March 16, 2026.
gallery.alt: Blue walls and white trim surround a worn brown wood floor, with a shop vacuum in the room.

gallery.caption: Hand tools and lifted finish at the edge of the original floor, March 16, 2026.
gallery.alt: Scrapers and curled finish shavings lie on wood flooring beside a floor register and white baseboard.

introduction: A former living room in the author's 1894 home is becoming a dedicated ballet barre studio. Original floorboards and shiplap remain central to the room, joined by reclaimed ceiling repairs, white mineral finishes, and carefully fitted crown molding.
evidenceBoundary: This account follows the journal through August 30, 2026. Final studio sign-off is not documented there. Three selected Studio photographs show the early room, floor work, and the room nearing completion; they do not establish final sign-off or an installed barre. The linked album photo count is a saved inventory value, not a live count.
